decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display that stays very close to our core POS-display knowledge, we can continue to refine it through existing design, production, and in-house R&D capabilities rather than withdraw it.

The pegboard-back display remains strongly related to our established cardboard display platform, so customer feedback and internal learning still support keeping it, though it faces some portfolio rationalisation risk.

This generic quarter-pallet display fits our competence base well, but because it overlaps most with nearby variants in a narrow product range, its withdrawal risk is higher even though we would presently retain it.

The eighth-pallet format is a clear, familiar extension of our display business and can be evaluated and improved with existing commercial and technical knowledge, making retention the more likely choice.

The media-focused quarter-pallet display still draws on our core cardboard display capabilities, but its more specialised application and overlap with other quarter-pallet offers raise the chance of later consolidation rather than immediate exit.
